title: Dedicated Capacity: Roadmap for Latency-Sensitive Verticals and Predictive Prewarm Strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and execute a focused quarter-long roadmap to ensure dedicated pools meet strict SLAs for latency-sensitive vertical customers (finance, healthcare) by combining predictive prewarm, targeted canaries, and adaptive autoscaling policies. Deliver a repeatable playbook and tooling that ops and solutions engineers can apply per-customer profile.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive prewarm model deployed to staging that reduces cold-start tail latency by >=30% for a 99th-percentile 4k token traffic profile
Two vertical-specific canaries (finance, healthcare) run for 2 weeks with monitored rollout metrics and rollback hooks
Console exposes per-route prewarm configuration and estimated cost delta in UI/runbook
Runbook and handoff completed for Support and Solutions Engineering with 90-minute incident play for capacity outages
Cross-team playbook published in Confluence and linked from customer onboarding checklist
notes: We observed recurring latency spikes for enterprise banking workloads during end-of-day batch-like bursts; root cause analysis points to cold model kernel contention + slow pool spin-up.
Priority is to reduce customer-visible p99 latency and remove need for manual warm-ups by Solutions Eng.
This initiative will be delivered as a set of experiments: forecast-driven prewarming, lightweight standby instances (micro-warm), and graceful throttling/fallback tiers.
Estimate covers product scoping, two eng spikes (forecast model + platform hooks), a console surface, and SRE runbook creation. Design is scoped for minimal UI work: toggle + cost estimate.
We will coordinate with Sales on at-risk customers to plan canary enrollments and communications; Jordan Blake will map the customer list.

Decisions so far: prefer a demand-forecast model anchored on recent usage windows (12–72h) rather than daily cron heuristics. We'll start with a simple exponential-smoothing baseline to limit operational complexity.

progress_updates: 2026-02-12 — Kickoff: alignment meeting with SRE, runtime, DS, Console. Agreed success metrics and canary targets.
2026-02-22 — ENG-21487 spike completed: tracing added to cold-start codepaths; initial p95/p99 breakdowns show contribution from kernel warm-up.
2026-03-02 — DS prototype (exponential smoothing) produced 28% predicted reduction in estimated cold-starts during sample week; needs staging validation.
2026-03-05 — Console prototype wireframe reviewed; Design requests clarifying copy around cost trade-offs (Design: Luis Ortega).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Forecast model underpredicts sudden bursts leading to missed SLAs. Mitigation: conservative headroom in prewarm counts + rapid fallback to cheaper burst pool with throttling.
Risk: Cost increases from overly aggressive prewarm. Mitigation: per-customer cost delta displayed in console and prewarm budgets with alerting; rollbacks when cost exceeds threshold.
Risk: Rollout complexity for regulated customers (healthcare). Mitigation: require Security review on canary config for PHI-handling customers and conduct tabletop exercises with Compliance.
Risk: Platform scalability of standby micro-instances. Mitigation: limit to verified verticals initially and instrument resource accounting; add autoscale guardrails per pool.
